extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and attorneys involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural outcomes governing disciplinary proceedings for attorneys registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, including grounds for discipline, required publications, and sanctions. Focuses on settlement approval, public reprimand, and the Office's authority to consider prior conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney registered to practice before the Office is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.; the USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters and authority to approve settlement agreements pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'At all times relevant hereto, Respondent ... has been an attorney registered (Registration No. 42,185) to practice before the Office and is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.' and 'The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter and the authority to approve the Agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline — conduct adversely reflects on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects upon a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office is a basis for discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by engaging in conduct that adversely reflects upon his fitness to practice before the Office.' The stipulated factual basis included a state-court-related plea of nolo contendere to battery and a State Bar public reproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state-bar or criminal proceedings as disciplinary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: State bar discipline and criminal pleas/admissions can serve as the factual basis for USPTO disciplinary action against a registered practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the order: The State Bar Court of California entered a Stipulated Reproval Order publicly reprimanding Respondent based on his plea of nolo contendere to a violation of California Penal Code section 242/243, subdivision (a) (battery), reported to Child Protective Services. Even though the Superior Court later expunged the conviction and terminated probation, the state action supported USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction — public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: A public reprimand is an authorized sanction the Office may impose (here by agreement) for conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded.' The sanction was part of a settlement agreement approved by the Under Secretary/Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement — OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders in disciplinary matters must be published electronically in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/.../OEDReadingRoom.jsp.' The Order mandates posting of the disciplinary decision in the OED repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement — Official Gazette notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette containing the practitioner's name, registration number, the regulation violated, and a summary of the underlying state/court action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Reprimand' followed by a multi-paragraph summary that includes: practitioner identification, citation to 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6), the State Bar Stipulated Order of Reproval, details of the criminal plea and reporting to Child Protective Services, and the Superior Court's expungement/termination of probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on future proceedings — consideration and aggravation/rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of a disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) may be considered by the Office in addressing further complaints of the same or similar misconduct and in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Nothing in the Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent ... and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding concerning Respondent (a) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to the settlement each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' No fee-shifting or additional monetary fine is ordered in this settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement approval statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement agreements resolving USPTO disciplinary action are approved under statutory and regulatory authority cited in the Order (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26, 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording in the Notice: 'This action is the result of a settlement agreement between Mr. Tikku and the OED Director pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.26 and 11.59.' The Order ties the enforcement mechanism and publication duties to those regulatory provisions.
